got_right: Randomised 11 interventions against a shared control with a registered plan (AsPredicted #151,281), using Lin covariate adjustment and HC2 SEs. This gives a clean, comparable arm-by-arm estimate on four outcomes.
Reported every arm for every outcome with CIs, and said plainly that the 44 registered tests were uncorrected and the pooled effect on accuracy was null (+1.0 point, SE 0.7, p = 0.132).

Split accuracy into AI-post detection and authentic-post recognition, and flagged the split as post hoc. This exposes a possible response-bias pattern: Breathing Exercise +9.1 points on detection with authentic recognition −4.8, and Infographic 2 −6.1 on authentic.
Included self-reported confidence and trust alongside accuracy, so the study can show calibration or backfire effects such as Inoculation raising confidence by 0.51 with no accuracy gain.

why_it_did_not_land.detail: Per-arm MDEs on accuracy are 3.2 to 5.2 points, about as large as the only significant effects. The significant arms are therefore likely overestimates, and the small arms cannot rule out realistic effects.
why_it_did_not_land.evidence: Power table H1: MDE 0.0318 (Nudge) to 0.0517 (Inoculation, n=78); Automated Flagging 0.044 vs MDE 0.042; Guide 0.047 vs MDE 0.039.

why_it_did_not_land.detail: Three of 11 accuracy arms cross p<0.05 with no multiplicity correction. Guide (p=0.043) and Mindfulness (p=0.032) would not survive any correction, and only Automated Flagging (p=0.004) is arguably robust. The pooled null contradicts a broad effect.
why_it_did_not_land.evidence: H1 table; pooled +0.010, p=0.132; 44 registered tests uncorrected.

why_it_did_not_land.detail: Total accuracy mixes detecting AI posts with accepting real ones, so a shift in scepticism looks like discernment gain or loss. Discernment (sensitivity) and bias were never separated, and the split outcomes were unregistered.
why_it_did_not_land.evidence: H5 Breathing +0.091 on AI posts but H6 −0.048 on real posts, with H1 only +0.015.

why_it_did_not_land.detail: Arms vary in content, dose and timing (labels in the feed vs pre-feed exercises), and the design cannot say which component works. Arm sizes are unbalanced (78 to 333) against a control of 181, and some data were collected before registration.
why_it_did_not_land.evidence: Arms ranged 78–333 against n=181 control; registration note on batches 1–2.

why_it_did_not_land.detail: The literature retrieved is almost entirely off-topic, so the study is not positioned against prior work on inoculation, accuracy nudges or AI-detection literacy. The only live framing, i-frame versus s-frame, is not something the design tests.
why_it_did_not_land.evidence: Related work: only Chater & Loewenstein and Ruggeri et al. are relevant; no AI-detection papers retrieved.

debates.label: Individual-level (i-frame) fixes vs system-level (s-frame) change
debates.position_a: Cheap individual-level interventions such as labels, nudges and literacy content can measurably improve people's handling of AI-generated media.
debates.position_b: Individual-level levers yield small, inconsistent effects, and meaningful change needs system-level measures such as platform-level or provenance infrastructure.
debates.what_this_study_says: Leans to b for educational and mindfulness-type interventions: pooled accuracy +1.0 point (p=0.132), with several arms null or harmful. Automated Flagging (+4.4), a system-supplied label, is the clearest gain, which weakly fits the s-frame view. The study cannot test system-level effects.

briefs.title: Separating discernment from response bias in machine-label interventions
briefs.question: Does Automated Flagging improve true discernment (sensitivity) rather than just shifting willingness to call posts AI-generated?
briefs.why_this_fixes_the_failure: Fixes measurement and power. It registers signal-detection outcomes (d′ and criterion) and replicates the one robust arm with an adequate sample.
briefs.design_sketch: Arms: Control, Automated Flagging, and Automated Flagging with 80% label accuracy versus 100%, plus a Guide arm as the best-performing education comparator. Respondents judge 40 posts balanced real and AI, with a confidence rating per post. Outcomes are d′, criterion and total accuracy, all registered, with Holm correction across arms. A US online panel with a pre-feed attention check.

power_target.basis: H1 Automated Flagging estimate 0.044, observed SD ~0.13; 80% power for ~0.04 needs ~165 per arm, inflated for Holm correction and the weaker label-accuracy arms

briefs.title: Individual literacy vs system-supplied cue: which carries the effect?
briefs.question: Is the accuracy gain from machine labels due to external information (s-frame) or to changed individual vigilance (i-frame)?
briefs.why_this_fixes_the_failure: Fixes design confounding: it separates cue content from attention or priming effects, which the original arms bundled.
briefs.design_sketch: 2x2 between-subjects: label present or absent, crossed with literacy training (Guide) present or absent, plus a placebo-label arm showing uninformative labels. If gain comes only with real labels, the s-frame reading is supported; if training alone or the placebo helps, vigilance explains it. Outcomes are accuracy and d′ on 40 posts.

power_target.basis: H1 MDE for n≈290 vs 181 arms was 0.034; interaction contrast needs the larger cells

briefs.title: Does the label effect hold for newer generators and low-trust respondents?
briefs.question: Does the Automated Flagging gain persist across stimulus realism (older vs current-generation synthetic media) and baseline media trust?
briefs.why_this_fixes_the_failure: Fixes sample and stimulus limits: the 2023 stimuli and US panel may not generalise, and the pooled null may hide moderation.
briefs.design_sketch: Control vs Automated Flagging, with the post set randomised between 2023-era and current-generation synthetic images and video. Media trust and AI familiarity are measured pre-treatment and used as registered moderators. Outcomes are accuracy and d′, with a re-contact two weeks later for durability on a subsample.
briefs.moderator_or_condition: Generator realism (2023 vs current) and baseline media trust (pre-registered median split)

power_target.basis: Interaction effects need roughly 4x the n of the main effect 0.044; MDE for the 0.0318–0.042 range in H1

verdict: A follow-up is worth running, but narrowly: only Automated Flagging (+4.4, p=0.004) looks like a real accuracy gain, and the pooled null (+1.0) and uncorrected tests warn against reading the rest. Run advance_design first. It replicates the label effect at adequate power and splits discernment from bias, which the current total accuracy score cannot do. The literature retrieved is mostly off-topic, so the only live debate is the i-frame versus s-frame framing, and the second brief tests it only indirectly.
